audit_result.proof_trace: The admin page issues an unbounded SELECT on `members` via `createClient()` (anon key + cookie JWT, RLS applies) with no per-user row filter, meaning the RLS USING clause must permit all authenticated users to read all rows — or uses an admin-aware DB-level check. No SQL files exist in the repository to verify which case holds; admin enforcement is implemented exclusively at the Next.js application layer (`admin/layout.tsx:18-24`, `checkAdmin()` in `members.ts:60-67`), not as a Supabase DB-level RLS guard. The overall codebase pattern (all 11 RPC functions lack `auth.uid()` checks, consistent app-layer-only enforcement) makes a permissive `USING (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL)` policy the more likely implementation.
audit_result.attack_scenario: An authenticated non-admin member with a valid session JWT (obtained via normal Discord login) calls `GET https://{project}.supabase.co/rest/v1/members?select=*` with `apikey: {anon_key}` (publicly visible in the client bundle) and `Authorization: Bearer {session_jwt}`, bypassing the Next.js admin layout check entirely and receiving all members' records including names, student numbers, Discord UIDs, and `is_admin` flags.

PROP-e5782b58-asm-001.text: RLS policies must enforce that non-admin users cannot read other users' member records.
PROP-e5782b58-asm-001.assertion: forall SELECT on members.users by user u: u.is_admin == false => row.id == u.id
